events.title: Proposed ruling: no_action (model confidence 0.85)
events.body:
The trip was a RydeTAXI metered trip, so the fare is meter-based and deviation mileage does feed the fare, and every off-route segment must be tested against RD-3/RD-4/RD-5 [F6][RD-2]. The only off-route segment is 12:27–12:36, where 5.86 km was driven against 2.69 km optimal, adding 3.17 km [F3][RD-1].

The determinative question is the scope of the rider's consent under RD-5 [F3][RD-5]. Before leaving the optimal route, at 12:24 the driver named both the reason and the corridor: "Traffic ahead on Pan Island Expressway is building up, ok if I go round via Sims Avenue?" [F7][RD-5]. The rider replied "Sure, go ahead" at 12:24, i.e. before the segment began at 12:27 [F8][RD-5]. The driver's statement matches the chat record [F9]. The route actually driven (toward Sims Avenue / the Geylang–Bedok corridor, ending at Bedok Mall) is consistent with the corridor named; nothing in the facts shows the car went somewhere other than what was named, so the consent is not stretched beyond its scope [F3][F7][RD-5]. The segment is therefore exempt.

RD-3(b) is not applicable in the driver's favour analysis here: it concerns rider-requested stops, not a driver-proposed, rider-agreed route change, so it cannot be used to defeat the RD-5 exemption [F3][RD-3].

RD-4 does not exempt the segment on traffic grounds: there is no LTA incident on the replaced optimal stretch [F12][RD-4], and a speed band alone (PIE and CTE at band 4, i.e. 30–39 km/h, which is not band 1 or 2) cannot independently exempt a segment [F10][F11][RD-4].

Since the sole off-route segment is fully exempt under RD-5, there is no non-exempt segment and the RD-2 refund formula yields 0 × $1.41/km = $0.00 [F3][F4][RD-2]. RD-6 is not triggered because the driver has no prior upheld route dispute in 90 days [F15][RD-6]. Both briefs request no_action, which is consistent with the trace outcome set.
